questions.q: A sample contains mixture of helium and oxygen gas. The ratio of root mean square speed of helium and oxygen in the sample, is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{ms}}=\sqrt{\frac{3 \mathrm{RT}}{\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{w}}}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{O}_2}}{\mathrm{~V}_{\mathrm{He}}}=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{w}, \mathrm{He}}}{\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{w}, \mathrm{O}_2}}} \\ & =\sqrt{\frac{4}{32}}=\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{2}} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{He}}}{\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{O}_2}}=\frac{2 \sqrt{2}}{1} \\ & \end{aligned}$

questions.q: A diatomic gas, having ${C}_{P} = \dfrac{7}{2}R$~and ${C}_{V} = \dfrac{5}{2}R,$~is heated at constant pressure. The ratio $dU: dQ: dW$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$dU = n{C}_{v}dT⇒ dQ = n{C}_{p}dT⇒ dW = PdV = nRdT$ (isobaric process)

$dU: dQ: dW: {C}_{v}: {C}_{p}: R= \dfrac{5R}{2}: \dfrac{7R}{2}: R = 5: 7: 2$.

questions.subject: Physics

questions.q: Let ${γ}_{1}$ be the ratio of molar specific heat at constant pressure and molar specific heat at constant volume of a monoatomic gas and~${γ}_{2}$~be the similar ratio of diatomic gas. Considering the diatomic gas molecule as a rigid rotator, the ratio~$\dfrac{\gamma1}{\gamma2}$& is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know,& ${C}_{v} = f\dfrac{R}{2}$

and~${C}_{p} = {C}_{v} + R = f\dfrac{R}{2} + R$

Therefore,~$\gamma = \dfrac{Cp}{Cv} = 1 + \dfrac{2}{f}$

For monatomic gas,~$f = 3$~and hence~${γ}_{1} = \dfrac{5}{3}$

For diatomic gas, $f = 5$~and hence~${γ}_{2} = \dfrac{7}{5}$

Required ratio,~$\dfrac{\gamma1}{\gamma2} = \dfrac{25}{21}$

questions.q: A mixture of 2 moles of helium gas (atomic mass = 4u) , and 1 mole of argon gas (atomic mass = 40 u) is kept at $300K$ in a container. The ratio of their rms speeds \left[\dfrac{{V}_{rms}\left(helium\right)}{{V}_{rms} ( argon )}\right],$ is close to:$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Using $V_{\mathrm{rms}}=\sqrt{\frac{3 R T}{M}} \Rightarrow V_{r m s} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{M}}\frac{v_{\text {rms (helium) }}}{v_{\text {rms (argon) }}}=\sqrt{\frac{M_{\text {argon }}}{M_{\text {helium }}}}=\sqrt{\frac{40}{4}}=\sqrt{10} \approx 3.16$

questions.q: Two ideal polyatomic gases at temperatures ${T}_{1}$ and ${T}_{2}$ are mixed so that there is no loss of energy. If ${F}_{1}$ and ${F}_{2}, {m}_{1}$ and ${m}_{2}, {n}_{1}$ and ${n}_{2}$ be the degrees of freedom, masses, number of molecules of the first and second gas respectively, the temperature of mixture of these two gases is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the final temperature of the mixture be $T .$

Since, there is no loss in energy.

$\Delta U = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{F1}{2}{n}_{1}R\Delta T + \dfrac{F2}{2}{n}_{2}R\Delta T = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{F1}{2}{n}_{1}R\left({T}_{1} - T\right) + \dfrac{F2}{2}{n}_{2}R\left({T}_{2} - T\right) = 0$

$⇒ T = \dfrac{{F}_{1}{n}_{1}R{T}_{1} + {F}_{2}{n}_{2}R{T}_{2}}{{F}_{1}{n}_{1}R + {F}_{2}{n}_{2}R} = \dfrac{{F}_{1}{n}_{1}{T}_{1} + {F}_{2}{n}_{2}{T}_{2}}{{F}_{1}{n}_{1} + {F}_{2}{n}_{2}}$

questions.q: Two thermodynamical process are shown in the figure. The molar heat capacity for process $A$ and $B$ are ${C}_{A}$ and ${C}_{B}$. The molar heat capacity at constant pressure and constant volume are represented by ${C}_{P}$ and ${C}_{V}$, respectively. Choose the correct statement.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For process $A$:

$logP = \gamma logV ⇒ P = V^{γ}, ( \gamma > 1 )$

$PV^{- \gamma} =$ Constant

${C}_{A} = {C}_{V} + \dfrac{R}{1 + \gamma} \ldots \left(i\right)$

Likewise, for process $B \to PV^{- 1} =$ Constant

${C}_{B} = {C}_{v} + $\dfrac{R}{1 + 1}

${C}_{B} = {C}_{v} + $\dfrac{R}{2} \ldots \left(ii\right)$

Also, ${C}_{P} = {C}_{v} + R \ldots \left(iii\right)$

By \left(ii\right)$ and \left(iii\right)$, we get

${C}_{P} > {C}_{B} > {C}_{v}$

$

questions.q:
Same gas is filled in two vessels of the same volume at the same temperature. If the ratio of the number of molecules is $1: 4$, then

$A$.~The r.m.s. velocity of gas molecules in two vessels will be the same.

$B$. The ratio of pressure in these vessels will be $1: 4$.

$C$. The ratio of pressure will be $1: 1$.

$D$. The r.m.s. velocity of gas molecules in two vessels will be in the ratio of~$1: 4$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The rms velocity of a gas is given by& ${V}_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$. Therefore,${V}_{rms}$~is~independent of number of moles, Hence, statement A is correct~and D is incorrect.

According to the ideal gas equation~$PV = nRT ⇒ P ∝ n$

$⇒ \dfrac{P1}{P2} = \dfrac{n1}{{n}_{2}} = \dfrac{1}{4}$

Hence, statement B is correct and C is incorrect.

Ans~[$A \text{ and } B$ only are correct]

questions.q: On the basis of kinetic theory of gases, the gas exerts pressure because its molecules:
options: continuously stick to the walls of container.
suffer change in momentum when impinge on the walls of container.
continuously lose their energy till it reaches wall.
are attracted by the walls of container.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: From the assumption of KTG, the molecules of gas collide with the walls and suffers momentum change which results in force on the wall and hence pressure.

questions.q: A bullet of mass $5gram$, travelling with a speed of $210ms^{- 1}$~strikes a fixed wooden target. One half of its kinetic energy is converted into heat in the wood. The rise of temperature of the bullet if the specific heat of its material is ~$0 . 030 \left(gram ° C\right)- 1  \left($1calorie = 4 .2 $\times {10}^{7}$ergs\right)$ close to :$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As per given condition Half of kinetic energy is transferred into heat energy and raises the temperature of bullet

$\dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} = ms\Delta T$

$\Deltat = \dfrac{V2}{4s}$

$= \dfrac{210 \times 210}{4 \times 4 . 2 \times 0 . 3 \times 1000} = 87 . 5 ° C$

questions.q: If the r.m.s speed of chlorine molecule is $490ms^{- 1}$ at ${27}^{o}C$, the r.m.s speed of argon molecules at the same temperature will be (Atomic mass of argon $= 39 . 9u$, molecular mass of chlorine $= 70 . 9u$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the rms speed of the argon molecules is given by

${v}_{Ar} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{MAr}} . . . \left(1\right)$

The formula to calculate the rms speed of chlorine molecule is given by

${v}_{Cl} = $\sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{MCl}} . . . \left(2\right)$

Divide equation (1) by equation (2) and simplify to obtain the required ratio.

\dfrac{vAr}{vCl} = \sqrt{\dfrac{MCl}{MAr}} . . . \left(3\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (3) and solve to calculate the required value.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{vAr}{490ms^{- 1}}& = & \sqrt{\dfrac{71}{40}}\\ & ⇒ & {v}_{Ar} = \sqrt{\dfrac{71}{40}} \times490ms^{- 1} \\ & \approx \text{ and } 651 . 7ms^{- 1}\end{cases}

$

questions.q: A gas mixture consists of 3 moles of oxygen and 5 moles of argon at temperature T. Considering only translational and rotational modes, the total internal energy of the system is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $U=\frac{f_{1}}{2} n_{1} R T+\frac{f_{2}}{2} n_{2} R T$ Considering translational and rotational modes, degrees of freedom $\mathrm{f}_{1}=5$ and $\mathrm{f}_{2}=3\therefore \mathrm{u}=\frac{5}{2}(3 \mathrm{RT})+\frac{3}{2} \times 5 \mathrm{RT}\mathrm{U}=15 \mathrm{RT}$

questions.q: At which temperature the r.m.s. velocity of a hydrogen molecule equal to that of an oxygen molecule at $47 ° C$ ?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The r.m.s velocity of the molecule of a gas of molecular weight $M$ at Kelvin temperature $T$is given by, ${V}_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$.

Let ${M}_{O}$ and ${M}_{H}$ are molecular weight of oxygen and hydrogen and ${T}_{O}$ and ${T}_{H}$ the corresponding Kelvin temperature at which ${V}_{r . m . s}$ is same for both,

${V}_{r . m . s} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3R{T}_{O}}{MO}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3R{T}_{H}}{MH}}$. Hence $\dfrac{TO}{MO} = \dfrac{TH}{MH}$

${T}_{O} = 273 ° C + 47 ° C = 320K$,

${M}_{O} = 32$,

${M}_{H} = 2 ⇒ {T}_{H} = \dfrac{2}{32} \times 320 = 20K$

questions.solution:
$f = 4 + 3 + 3 = 10$, assuming non-linear,~

questions.q:
The $r$ ms speed of oxygen molecule in a vessel at particular temperature is~\left(1 + \dfrac{5}{x}\right)\dfrac{1}{2}v,$~when~$v$~is the average speed of the molecule. The value of~$x$~will be:

(take $\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}$)

$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The RMS speed is given by&

${v}_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$

The average speed is given by~

${v}_{avg} = \sqrt{\dfrac{8RT}{\piM}}$

The ratio is~

$⇒ \dfrac{vrms}{v\text{avg}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}{\dfrac{8RT}{\piM}} =}\sqrt{\dfrac{3\pi}{8}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{8} \times \dfrac{22}{7}} ⇒ \dfrac{vrms}{v\text{avg}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{33}{28}}$

Comparing it with the given value~\left(1 + \dfrac{5}{x}\right)\dfrac{1}{2}$,

$\dfrac{vrms}{v\text{avg}} = \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{5}{28}} ⇒ x = 28$

$

questions.q: The ratio of specific heats  \left(\dfrac{CP}{CV}\right)$ in terms of degree of freedom  \left(f\right)$ is given by :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From Mayer's relation& ${C}_{P} = {C}_{V} + R$~and~${C}_{V} = \dfrac{f}{2}R$

Ratio of specific heat,

$\gamma = \dfrac{CP}{CV} = 1 + \dfrac{R}{\dfrac{f}{2}R} = 1 + \dfrac{2}{f}$

questions.q: If the root mean square velocity of hydrogen molecule at a given temperature and pressure is $2kms^{- 1},$ the root mean square velocity of oxygen at the same condition in $kms^{- 1}$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Root mean square velocity is given by, ${V}_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$

Therefore, $\dfrac{V1}{{V}_{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{M2}{M1}} ⇒ \dfrac{2}{{V}_{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{32}{2}}$

$⇒ {V}_{2} = 0 . 5kms^{- 1}$

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:

List I List II
(A) $3$~Translational degrees of freedom (I) Monoatomic gases
(B) $3$ Translational, $2$ rotational degrees of freedoms (II) Polyatomic gases
(C) $3$ Translational, $2$ rotational and $1$ vibrational degrees of freedom (III) Rigid diatomic gases
(D) $3$ Translational, $3$ rotational and more than one vibrational degrees of freedom (IV) Nonrigid diatomic gases

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula for degree of freedom is given by&

$f = 3N - k$

where~$N$~is the number of particles,~$k$~is the individual relationship in the system.

For a monoatomic~gas particle,~$N = 1, k = 0$. So,~$f = 3$

Hence, monoatomic gas has $3$ translational degree of freedom.

For a rigid diatomic gas molecule, there are~$5$~degrees of freedom,~$3$~translational and~$2$~rotational.~A diatomic gas can have two extra degrees of freedom due to rotation along two independent axes.

A non rigid diatomic molecule has one extra degree of freedom than a rigid one. This is the vibrational degree of freedom. Hence, it has~$6$~degrees of freedom.

So, a~non rigid diatomic gas has~$3$ translational,~$2$ rotational and~$1$ vibrational degrees of freedom.

A polyatomic gas has more than two atoms per molecule. Hence, the total number of degrees of freedom is~$3$ translational, $3$ rotational and more than one vibrational degree of freedom.

questions.q: If the R.M.S. speed of oxygen molecules at $0 ° C$ is $160ms^{- 1}$. Find the R.M.S. speed of hydrogen molecules at $0 ° C$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Recall the formula of root mean& square speed,& ${v}_{RMS} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$,~

$⇒ \dfrac{\left({v}_{RMS}\right){O}_{2}}{\left({v}_{RMS}\right){H}_{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{M{H}_{2}}{M{O}_{2}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{32}} = \dfrac{1}{4}$

$⇒ \left({v}_{RMS}\right){H}_{2} = 4\left({v}_{RMS}\right){O}_{2} = 4 \times 160 = 640{m s}^{- 1}$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The temperature of a gas is $- 73 ° C$. When the gas is heated to $527 ° C$, the root mean square speed of the molecules is doubled.
Statement II : The product of pressure and volume of an ideal gas will be equal to translational kinetic energy of the molecules.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The given reactant is phenyl benzyl ether ($C_6H_5-O-CH_2-C_6H_5$).

When it reacts with $HI$, the ether oxygen is first protonated to form an oxonium ion. The cleavage of the ether linkage then takes place.

The $C_6H_5-O$ bond has partial double bond character due to the resonance of the oxygen's lone pair with the benzene ring, making it strong and difficult to break. On the other hand, the $O-CH_2$ bond is a weaker single bond. Moreover, cleavage of the $O-CH_2$ bond can proceed via a highly stable benzyl carbocation (in an $S_N1$ mechanism) or undergo facile $S_N2$ attack by the iodide ion ($I^-$) at the less sterically hindered and activated benzylic carbon.

Therefore, the $I^-$ ion attacks the $CH_2$ group, cleaving the $O-CH_2$ bond. The products formed are phenol ($C_6H_5OH$) and benzyl iodide ($C_6H_5CH_2I$).

Statement I claims the products are benzyl alcohol and iodobenzene, which is incorrect. Thus, Statement I is false.

Statement II claims that the $-O-CH_2-$ bond is cleaved to give the product, which is correct. Thus, Statement II is true.

Answer: Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.q: $N$ moles of a polyatomic gas$( f = 6 )$ must be mixed with two moles of a monoatomic gas so that the mixture behaves as a diatomic gas. The value of $N$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The equivalent degree of freedom ${f}_{eq}$ of the mixture is

${f}_{eq} = \dfrac{{n}_{1}{f}_{1} + {n}_{2}{f}_{2}}{{n}_{1} + {n}_{2}}$

For diatomic gas ${f}_{eq} = 5$.

$⇒ 5 = \dfrac{( n ) ( 6 ) + ( 2 ) ( 3 )}{n + 2}$

$⇒ 5n + 10 = 6n + 6$

$⇒ n = 4$

questions.q: The specific heat at constant pressure of a real gas obeying $P V^2=R T$ equation is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{dQ}=\mathrm{du}+\mathrm{dW} \\ & \mathrm{CdT}=\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{V}} \mathrm{dT}+\mathrm{PdV} \\ & \therefore \mathrm{PV}^2=\mathrm{RT} \\ & \mathrm{P}=\text { constant } \\ & \mathrm{P}(2 \mathrm{VdV})=\mathrm{RdT} \\ & \mathrm{PdV}=\frac{\mathrm{RdT}}{2 \mathrm{~V}} \\ & \end{aligned}$
Put in equation (1) $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{V}}+\frac{\mathrm{R}}{2 \mathrm{~V}}$

questions.q: The R.M.S. speeds of the molecules of Hydrogen, Oxygen, and Carbon dioxide& at the same temperature are ${v}_{H}, {v}_{O}$ and ${v}_{C}$ respectively, then:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: The formula of root-mean-square speed in terms of absolute temperature and molecular mass of the gas& is,& ${v}_{RMS} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}} ⇒ {v}_{RMS} ∝ \dfrac{1}{M}$, here we know that,~${M}_{H2} < {M}_{O2} < {M}_{CO2}⇒ {v}_{H} > {v}_{O} > {v}_{C}$.
